…registry

Raw SAVEPOINT/RELEASE SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT SQL from the Drizzle
client was passed through to conn.execute() as plain statements. After a
DBAPI error, SQLAlchemy raises PendingRollbackError on the connection and
raw savepoint statements cannot recover it.

TransactionRegistry.execute() now recognizes these three statement forms
(case-insensitive, optional trailing semicolon) and maps them onto
SQLAlchemy's conn.begin_nested() instead, tracking a per-session stack of
open savepoints on _Held. ROLLBACK TO unwinds and resolves everything above
and including the named savepoint (LIFO); an unknown name raises ValueError.
_drop() resolves any still-open savepoints before finalizing the root
transaction so commit/rollback never leaves a nested transaction dangling.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

… test

Two review fixes to the savepoint interception added in fd90a791:

1. _handle_savepoint's release/rollback branch deleted the unwound stack
   entries (del held.savepoints[i:]) before calling commit()/rollback() on
   them. If one of those calls raised mid-unwind, the already-deleted
   entries would be orphaned — _drop() would never see them again to clean
   up. Reordered to resolve each entry immediately before removing it, so
   an exception mid-unwind leaves the remaining unresolved entries on the
   stack for _drop() to finalize.

2. test_session_rollback_resolves_open_savepoints only asserted
   eng.last_conn.closed, which passes even if _drop()'s savepoint-resolution
   loop is removed entirely (conn.close() fires unconditionally in the
   finally). Added an assertion on eng.last_conn.nested[0].rolled_back so
   the test actually verifies the resolution behavior it is named for.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.messageBody:
…over

The execute() session-bound except-branch rolled back and discarded the
session on ANY failed statement, which made the client's compensating
rollback throw 'unknown or expired transaction session' (masking the
real SQL error) and made savepoint recovery (Task 1) impossible.

A failed statement now leaves the session open: Postgres marks the
transaction aborted (commit degrades to rollback), MySQL leaves it
usable. The client owns recovery via rollback or rollback to
savepoint; sessions still end via commit/rollback, close_all(), or
the idle reaper.

commits.messageBody:
to_sqlalchemy_text previously regex-rewrote every $<digits> across the
whole SQL string, corrupting literals like 'costs $1 per unit' in
Drizzle sql-template traffic, and raising an opaque IndexError on
out-of-range placeholder indices.

Replace the module-level _PLACEHOLDER regex substitution with a
character scanner (_rewrite_placeholders) that skips $n inside
single-quoted strings ('' doubling, E'...' backslash escapes),
double-quoted identifiers ("" doubling), dollar-quoted bodies
($$/$tag$), -- line comments, and nested /* */ block comments. An
index above len(params) now raises a clear ValueError instead of
corrupting output or crashing with IndexError.

Wrap the compensating rollback in PipesSession.transaction and the
rollback-to-savepoint statement in PipesTransaction.transaction in
try/catch that swallows recovery failures. Server-side changes now
keep failed statements' sessions alive so client rollback usually
succeeds, but it can still fail (transport down, session idle-reaped);
that failure must never replace the original SQL error the caller
needs to see.

…rows

PipesTransport.query now returns { rows, affectedRows }; the no-fields
execute() branch resolves to { rows, rowCount } (node-postgres parity)
instead of a bare row array, so writes without .returning() can report
a row count. PipesQueryResultHKT is generic over the row type (mirrors
NodePgQueryResultHKT over QueryResult) because drizzle's polymorphic
this['row'] can't appear nested inside a further object-type literal.

commits.messageBody:
…eries

DrizzleConfig.cache reached drizzle() but was dropped before PipesSession:
PipesPreparedQuery's super() call always passed undefined for cache and
queryMetadata, and PipesSession.prepareQuery discarded the queryMetadata/
cacheConfig args drizzle's own query builders pass it.

- PipesSessionOptions gains cache?: Cache; drizzle() forwards config.cache.
- PipesSession.prepareQuery forwards queryMetadata/cacheConfig through to
  PipesPreparedQuery, whose constructor now passes cache/queryMetadata/
  cacheConfig into super() instead of (undefined, undefined).
- PipesPreparedQuery.execute() routes transport calls through the inherited
  (internal, not in the published .d.ts) queryWithCache() so a configured
  cache is actually consulted, mirroring node-postgres/session.js.

queryWithCache also wraps query failures in DrizzleQueryError (upstream
behavior); updated the one test asserting on a raw transport error message
to check err.cause instead, since the original error is now preserved there.

Verified against the installed drizzle-orm 0.45.2 contract in node_modules
(pg-core/session.d.ts, node-postgres/session.d.ts/.js) rather than assumed.

Update the drizzle-over-pipes guide for behavior changed in tasks 1-8 of
this review-fix pass:

- Writes without .returning() resolve to { rows, rowCount } (node-postgres
  parity); add an optimistic-lock retry example on rowCount === 0.
- Query failures surface as drizzle's DrizzleQueryError (message does not
  include the cause text); show a catch example reading err.cause.
- Transaction error semantics: the original error is never replaced by a
  rollback failure; nested savepoint recovery now works for real SQL
  errors, not just JS throws; abandoned sessions are reaped after the
  server's idle timeout (300s default).
- Note that Buffer/bytea parameters aren't supported by the JSON
  transport (server-side bind error, not silent).
- Document the new cache parameter (DrizzleConfig.cache is now
  propagated to prepared queries).

Grepped other co-located docs for stale execute-tool row-shape prose
(row_mode/affected_rows); nodes/src/nodes/{db_postgres,db_mysql}/README.md
already describe the wire shape accurately, no changes needed there.
